Here is a notebook to help get you started working with the data from the Geo Remote project. Please do not edit this file, make a copy or copy code from it

## pacman
pacman - pacman is a helpful package we use to load other packages. Make sure it is installed.
```{r}
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
```

## scripts directory
The following code will set the working directory to the scripts directory. This is where the scripts for the Geo Remote project are stored. If the current working directory is not in the scripts directory, it will prompt you to select a file within the scripts directory. You can select any file, and it can be nested as long as it is within the scripts folder.
```{r}
# If your working directory is in the GeoRemote Scripts folder, it'll set the correct path. If it's not, it will ask you to select a file in the directory
if ("Scripts" %in% unlist(strsplit(normalizePath("."), "/"))) {
  scripts_directory = paste(unlist(strsplit(normalizePath("."), "/"))[1:which(unlist(strsplit(normalizePath("."), "/"))=="Scripts")],collapse="/")
} else {
  print("Select any file withing Scripts to set up the path")
  temp = file.choose()
  scripts_directory = paste(unlist(strsplit(temp, "/"))[1:which(unlist(strsplit(temp, "/"))=="Scripts")],collapse="/")
}
```

## Redcap
First, source the redcap utilities script. This will make the redcap utility functions available to you. Please use these scripts to load the redcap data. You can use whichever one you need, and comment the others out, or copy and paste into your script.

Redcap Codebook - You can open the redcap dictionary (or load it with the function below) to see what all of the redcap variables and their options are.
```{r}
source(file.path(scripts_directory, "Utility Scripts/geo_redcap.r"))

# Load redcap data  
redcap <- load_redcap()

# Load redcap dictionary - useful for subsetting surveys such as demographics_from_qualtrics, etc.
redcap_dictionary <- load_redcap_dictionary()

# If you need the raw redcap data for whatever reason, you can find that here:
raw_redcap <- load_raw_redcap()
```

## Lifedata/EMA
Use the script to load the ema data collected with lifedata. You can load the data in either long or wide format. 

Please note that in a wide format, variables will be NA for surveys they were not a part of. Please refer to the codebook to see what sessions contain what variables.

[EMA Codebook](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14TSq-rwDdnFKtVHk3SJJ7SnRjqRYZsy1O4XDSKmGgl8/edit?gid=1439201647#gid=1439201647)
If you need access to the codebook, please contact a member of the geo team.
Nicole Cooper - ncooper@falklab.org
Anthony Resnick - aresnick@falklab.org
Ally Paul - apaul@falklab.org

```{r}
source(file.path(scripts_directory, "Utility Scripts/geo_lifedata.r"))

# Load lifedata
lifedata = load_lifedata()

# Load wide lifedata
wide_lifedata = load_lifedata(format="wide")
```

# Qualtrics/Scored Surveys
To load the qualtrics data, use the geo_qualtrics.r script in the utilies folder. You can also use this to load the scored surveys.

QUALTRICS_SURVEY_IDS:
    "Cotinine_GeoRemote" = "SV_4Mmb2WuyZ8wi7CC"
    "GoogleMaps_Timeline_GeoRemote" = "SV_5clHlGytvXaeuQ6"
    "ImageTask_GeoRemote" = "SV_bjx9BR3c6r2zO98" 
    "LifeData_RealLifeExp_GeoRemote" = "SV_74yOXRfEikzv8bA"
    "SurveyMeasures_GeoRemote" = "SV_6mxadaCn4QKRwLc"
    "StudyInstructions_GeoRemote" = "SV_brsqXudHeEWyqOi"
  
```{r}
source(file.path(scripts_directory, "Utility Scripts/geo_qualtrics.r"))

# To download qualtrics surveys straight from qualtrics. If you haven't, you'll need to install your API key.
download_raw_qualtrics_surveys(surveys = "all",
                               save = FALSE, # TRUE to save to the server
                               save_qualtrics_credentials = TRUE) # Save your qualtrics credentials

# To load the raw qualtrics data (no cleaning, scoring, or filtering)
raw_surveys = load_surveys()
raw_surveys = load_surveys(survey_name="SurveyMeasures_GeoRemote")

# For clean surveys:
survey_measures = load_qualtrics_survey_measures()
weekly_surveys = load_qualtrics_weekly_surveys()
fmri_surveys = load_qualtrics_fmri_surveys()

# Load scored surveys:
bhv = load_scored_survey(scale_name = "BHV")
cosw_wide = load_scored_survey(scale_name = "COSW", type = "wide")
all_scored_measures = load_scored_survey(scale_name = "scored_Survey_Measures")

# You can filter by session or scale name if you load all the measures
cesd = all_scored_measures %>%
  filter(sm_session=='1',
         scale_name=='cesd') %>%
  # And if you want to pivot the data to wide format
  select(pid, sm_session, survey_name, scale_name, scored_scale, score) %>%
      pivot_wider(
        names_from = scored_scale,
        values_from = score
      )
```
